title: jobs search under basic-auth: non-admins only see jobs whose creator is them; creator-less jobs stay hidden
answers: Under basic-auth, can a non-admin user see other users' jobs through the job search endpoint?
Why does POST /ajax-api/3.0/jobs/search hide jobs that have no creator for non-admin users?
Where is the ownership filtering for native FastAPI job search implemented?
How does the job response expose the creator so search results can be scoped?
body:
Path: `POST /ajax-api/3.0/jobs/search`, the native FastAPI job listing that returns every job in the job store (no pagination) under `--app-name basic-auth`. The response passes through the auth middleware in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:fastapi_permission_middleware; the chokepoint is mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_filter_search_jobs.
Rule: `_filter_search_jobs` keeps only jobs whose `creator` equals the caller's username. It is registered in `FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS` keyed on mlflow/server/job_api.py:search_jobs. The `creator` field comes from mlflow/server/job_api.py:Job.from_job_entity, so the filter can see ownership. Jobs with no recorded creator are dropped for non-admins, matching the fail-closed ownership check on the per-id get/cancel routes.
Symptom: Any authenticated non-admin user who POSTed to jobs/search received every job's id, params, and result/error text, including other users' jobs, while GET /jobs/{job_id} returned 403 for the same foreign job.
Constraints: Admins skip response filters, so they keep the unfiltered listing including creator-less jobs. Creator-less jobs (rows predating the creator column, worker-spawned online-scoring child jobs) are invisible to non-admins in search. Post-response filtering is only complete because the search handler returns the full, unpaginated result set; if search gains pagination, the scope has to move into the store query.
applies: Basic-auth FastAPI job search route only; not the Flask job endpoints or the per-id get/cancel routes, which have their own ownership validator.
says: Standard users can see other team members' jobs and parameters in the jobs list.
Restrict the job search view so non-admin accounts only see their own submitted jobs.
The jobs table lists tasks that regular members receive permission denied errors opening.
Legacy jobs and worker scoring tasks are missing from search results for standard users.
search: Under basic-auth on POST /ajax-api/3.0/jobs/search, mlflow.server.auth._filter_search_jobs filters the native FastAPI job listing to drop jobs whose creator does not match the caller's username, as well as creator-less jobs, for non-admin users. The filter is registered in FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS for mlflow.server.job_api.search_jobs and executed via fastapi_permission_middleware using creator populated by Job.from_job_entity. Admins bypass response filters and retain the full listing, while Flask job endpoints and per-id routes use separate validators; filtering works post-response because search is unpaginated.
